requirements.title: A variable denotes a designator object or an associated pointer target
requirements.definition: A designator variable is the data object denoted by the designator. A function-reference variable is the target of the pointer produced by evaluating the function reference, and that pointer is required to be associated at the reference. The rule identifies the variable; it does not license reading an undefined target.

requirements.title: A variable reference is permitted only after the variable or data-pointer target is defined
requirements.definition: A reference to a variable is permitted only when the variable is defined. A reference to a data pointer is permitted only when the pointer is associated with a target object that is defined. The events that define variables with values are those described in 19.6.5; later undefinedness remains governed by 19.6.6.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_087.json reads all16 original 9.2 units and their28 fine units and confirms that R902-R907 and C901-C907 reuse the actual numbered identifiers and conditions. C901 excludes a constant and any subobject of a constant, including a substring of a literal constant through the R909 parent-string alternatives; C902 requires a data pointer result, which p1 complements by requiring that pointer to be associated. The four typed categories R904-R907 share the general variable grammar while their paired constraints impose type. S9.2-001 and S9.2-002 carry the identity and definedness effects with no diagnostic duty, since a reference to an undefined variable is generally not statically detectable, and their plans use positive controls with literal oracles instead of executing an undefined read. The unnumbered note stays informative. All38 facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
